links.note: Cost of a toy, exponential-time index calculus on fixed-cofactor curves; the measurement quantifies its distance to rho, it cannot establish a speedup.

question: On the three registered 16-bit fixed-cofactor curves toy_curve_with_cofactor(16, 20261021, c), c = 2, 4, 8 (r = 32843, 16411, 8231), what does the fixed-cofactor tensor-contraction index calculus (ic.tensor_contraction_cofactor_v1, m = 2) cost in S against the matched rho reference rho.negation, with the §5a band on unpriced native work?

claims.text: Every measured row of every arm recovers the planted scalar (verified by the harness).

Per curve (both shards pooled, 8 workloads), the paired ratio of summed S, tensor-cof-m2 over rho-neg, with its bootstrap interval and the §5a band (unpriced native work at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation on every arm).
claims.if_supported: a measured gap to rho on these three curves; no claim beyond them
claims.if_not_supported: the ratio interval includes 1 or the order flips inside the §5a band: no ranking

hypotheses.statement: The cofactor tensor arm costs far more than rho in S on every curve.
hypotheses.mechanism: As for the prime-order arm, each relation costs an exact contraction over about |F_1||F_2| ≈ 2r subgroup sums plus c preimages per member, and about 2(2r)^(1/2) relations are needed, so GAE grows like r^(3/2) and S like r; rho's S is about 1.

predictions.minimum_effect: ratio interval above 1 on every curve

data_seen.measured: descriptive wall time of single ic tensor demo --cofactor solves on random 12–16-bit curves of this container, used only to size the shards; no S count of any arm on the registered curves was seen

arms.description: rho.negation, the matched rho reference on prime curves
ic.tensor_contraction_cofactor_v1 with m = 2: whole-point cofactor network, preimages of each F_i listed once per draw
rho.negation repeated under a second arm name: the A/A noise floor

positive.not_applicable_reason: every workload carries a planted scalar and the harness checks [k]G = Q on every row; a miss is a wrong_answer row

negative.not_applicable_reason: a cost comparison between methods on the same instances asserts nothing about a null population

randomization.arm_order_reason: alternate_measured over one measured round, which ecbench cannot balance (plan warning accepted, as for the 2026-10-30 16-bit session); S is counted, not timed, so order cannot move it; the specs set ecbench order alternate_measured, recorded here as alternate (the schema's nearest value)

seed_derivation.note: ecbench derives algorithm_seed per execution from measurement.seed 20261107 and the plan

instance_sampling.rule: 4 targets per shard from target_seed 202611071 / 202611072 under the spec's target law, 8 per curve

blinding.how: not masked: arms are named by method in the harness output; the decision rule is fixed below before data

power.note: 8 workloads x 1 round per curve; S is deterministic per (workload, seed), so a replicate would repeat the same number

preflight_runtime.measured_on: descriptive single ic tensor demo --cofactor solves on this container after #3598: c = 2 r = 28657 402 s; c = 4 r = 11443 269 s; c = 8 r = 4799 157 s; scaled to the registered r: about 490, 460 and 350 s per tensor target, about 2000 s per 4-target shard; rho is sub-second

primary.name: S
primary.definition: every phase charged in ecbench.gae divided by sqrt(r)

secondary.name: unpriced native work
secondary.definition: each arm's *_uncharged counters, priced at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation for the §5a band

placement.note: one isolab-eks request per spec (six), each under the 3600 s job cap

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 6 sessions x 3 arms x 4 workloads x 1 round = 72 executions; then stop
a row whose answer does not verify stops nothing and is recorded as wrong_answer
a shard that hits the job cap is re-submitted once unchanged; a second cap leaves that curve inconclusive

invalidation_rules: a row with outcome.status other than verified is excluded from the decisive comparison and reported
a session whose audit is not OK with every replay identical yields no result
these sessions carry no wall-time claim at any isolation level
a curve with a missing or capped shard is inconclusive; the two shards are pooled only when both audit OK

decision_rule.text: Per curve, C2 is supported when the paired ratio of summed S tensor-cof-m2 over rho-neg, pooled over both shards (8 workloads), has a 95% bootstrap interval excluding 1 and the order holds at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per unpriced operation on every arm; otherwise no ranking on that curve. Holm correction over the three per-curve comparisons; C-aa is the noise floor, not a decision.
decision_rule.threshold: ratio interval excludes 1 across the §5a band
decision_rule.statistic: sum of S over (workload, round) pairs, ratio candidate/reference (ecbench compare)
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed S per curve

outputs: ecbench compare --a rho-neg --b tensor-cof-m2 (both shards of a curve)

graphs: S per arm per curve (log scale) against log2 r, with intervals
S ratio tensor-cof-m2 / rho-neg against c, with the §5a band

inadmissible: changing the workloads, seeds, shards, unit or accounting after seeing results
quoting wall time from these sessions as a result
reading a toy-size measurement as evidence about deployed curves (Ed25519 has cofactor 8 but is far beyond toy sizes)
calling any result a speedup: the counters are exponential

literature.claim: the counted unit S, isolation levels and paired comparison
the algorithm, its exponential counters and its limits
the fixed-cofactor setting, the c^m count identity and the network
